The lean annex and pitched shed form a lower silhouette behind the outdoor dispensing mortar. Plants remain legible in front of the brick and concrete versions. Binary LOD counts 1236/562/248.
The red-roofed ward blocks flank a taller admission bay and visible blue-and-white emblem. The flue breaks the rear skyline. The emblem has overlapping outward faces. Binary LOD counts 850/422/198.

models.observations: Two distinct teaching wings enclose a front court and bell tower. The bell, cap and blue pennant provide a center to both the terracotta and darker Medieval rows. Binary LOD counts 836/424/188.

The pale twin pavilions and tower frame a dark accessible court. Upper gallery, bright fittings and flag give the campus a common identity at all three levels of detail. Binary LOD counts 1046/550/276.
The double teaching wings and a stepped bell lantern remain readable across brick and concrete rows. The blue entrance awning marks the recessed courtyard doorway. Binary LOD counts 996/500/226.

The pale admissions cross has a crisp four-armed profile against the blue enamel under the terracotta roofs. Its joints are clean in all three LODs; the ward courts and flue still read. Reopened age previews at 224 and 64 px, and inspected serialized LODs at 80 px (850/422/198 triangles). Surface audit clear.

The enlarged cross on the tall admission bay remains visible under both the blue and gold roof palettes. The sign sits clear of the canopy, and both side wards keep their outline at LOD2. Ivory pages meet the spine cleanly and stand out against the book's dark cover. In all four age rows the codex is legible above the open-fronted stair, and the turret stays distinct in the distance. Reopened age previews at 224 and 64 px, and inspected serialized LODs at 80 px (733/406/182 triangles). Surface audit clear.

The ivory folio and bookbinding stand out against brick and steel at 64 px. The binding and pages stay in contact, with the step and low entry centered below. Reopened age previews at 224 and 64 px, and inspected serialized LODs at 80 px (787/426/208 triangles). Surface audit clear.

The larger white cross and royal-blue disc now sit against a broad glazed tier above the canopy. The cross is recognizable at phone scale even as the upper gallery trims simplify. Reopened age previews at 224 and 64 px, and inspected serialized LODs at 80 px (1030/528/198 triangles). Surface audit clear.

Reopened age previews at 224 and 64 px, and inspected serialized LODs at 80 px (1101/684/350 triangles). Surface audit clear.

Reopened age previews at 224 and 64 px, and inspected serialized LODs at 80 px (615/350/180 triangles). Surface audit clear.

An exterior instrument points at a small sample stage beside the cylindrical tower. A slate-roofed brick laboratory with an awning anchors the equipment, with clear gaps between the instrument and building. Serialized triangle counts are 921, 524, 292 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

models.observations: A rooftop pool over a glazed pavilion steps down to two lower pools. Blue water and a small planted entry mark the approach. The separate basins, terrace edges and central supporting pavilion remain visible at distance and read differently from the industrial bath shed.

A high brick flue rises beside a broad glazed barrel roof, with a low service housing along the furnace wall. Fine glazing ribs disappear at the middle distance. The deep vault, end wall and boiler stack retain the public bath profile from front and rear.

A long column-supported portico opens directly onto two divided medicinal beds. The beds expose more working area than the ancient hut, with an earthen jar by the door. They retain their raised frames and planting at the far level.

Three planting ledges spiral around a tall blue growing column, with an access hut at its base. The ledges can be seen meeting the core from the rear. At LOD2 they still carry visible greenery beneath the broad cap, distinct from the glasshouse and stone garden.

A tall roof vent stands above a brick processing house with a large copper vessel at the side and a herb bed in front. The side view exposes the vessel and its pipe next to the wall. The reduced mesh retains the herbs and distilling apparatus as separate forms.

A broad dish on a forked pedestal is unmistakable in both unpainted views. Its feed arms converge over the face while a small control room anchors the site. At LOD2 the dish perimeter facets simplify, but the pedestal and receiver still read from behind.

The projecting telescope barrel, broad pivot and stepped masonry pier create a different optical instrument from the future dish. A reading stand sits beside the service room. The mounting and tube survive the rear and distant views, including the open gap beneath the barrel.

A large cream web passes around the rollers at the front of a tall brick works. The open dark press frame gives the paper a clear backing. The upright shop and projecting paper feed read from both angles even after the far mesh loses individual windows.

Splayed external legs connect the high cap to a low base around a luminous test vessel. A separate flat-roofed control room sets its scale. The side and rear views retain the open frame and distinguish the apparatus from the earlier broad laboratory hall.

A rounded reading room with a hipped tiled cap projects beyond the small covered entry. The white leaves of an open book stand out against its lectern at the front. The round wall, porch and book remain legible at distance.

The stacked offset archive floors and blue clerestories make a stepped silhouette above an entrance desk. The end view shows the middle floor bearing on the central block. The far model retains its projected floors and the open book by the door.

A slim flagged entry tower steps above a long roof-lit brick writing hall. Its side view separates the open book from the doorway and the rear view exposes parallel roof ridges. The tower, ridges and book survive the distant mesh.
